target.body:

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where canceling an agent run while transcript live capture was starting could still let the provider start, persist transcript data, and register an active session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcripts tool now accepts the agent run's cancellation signal and forwards it to the pending live-capture start lifecycle. While startup is pending it rejects utterances delivered after cancellation and checks provider cleanup; if cleanup cannot be confirmed, it records a cleanup-pending active session so later stop attempts remain retryable until the provider confirms success. Once startup succeeds, the originating run signal no longer suppresses capture. Provider contracts, configuration, persistence formats, and ordinary stop-failure finalization are unchanged.

## User Impact

Stopping an agent run now prevents its pending transcript capture from writing content after cancellation. Successful provider cleanup leaves no active session; failed cleanup stays visible and retryable instead of becoming an untracked background capture.

## Evidence

- Focused pre-fix regressions proved the provider received `undefined`, late post-abort utterances were persisted, cleanup failures became untracked, and a run abort after successful startup could suppress an otherwise active transcript. After the fix, the complete transcripts tool test file passes: 13/13 tests.
- A local live E2E proof registered real transcript providers through the plugin capability registry, invoked the real agent tool/provider contract against a temporary state directory, canceled during provider startup, queried active sessions, inspected JSONL persistence, verified post-start capture continuity, and retried repeated cleanup failures:

```json

  "runSignalAborted": true,
  "providerReceivedAbortSignal": true,
  "toolResolved": false,
  "toolText": null,
  "toolError": "provider start aborted",
  "statusActive": [],
  "persistedTranscriptAfterAbort": null,
  "stopCallsBeforeCleanup": 0,
  "postStartCancellation": {
    "runSignalAborted": true,
    "providerReceivedAbortSignal": true,
    "persistedTranscriptAfterRunAbort": "captured after start completed and agent run ended"
  },
  "failedCleanup": {
    "providerReceivedAbortSignal": true,
    "toolError": "transcripts start aborted; provider cleanup failed: proof cleanup failed",
    "activeBeforeRetry": [{
      "sessionId": "cancelled-meeting-retry",
      "providerId": "proof-live-retry"
    }],
    "persistedTranscriptAfterAbort": null,
    "stopCallsBeforeRetry": 1,
    "failedRetryError": "transcripts provider cleanup failed: proof cleanup failed",
    "activeAfterFailedRetry": [{

      "cleanupPending": true
    }],
    "stopCallsAfterFailedRetry": 2,
    "stopCallsAfterRetry": 3,
    "activeAfterRetry": []

}
```

target.title: feat(ui): multi-select sessions in the sidebar with batch menu actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #104409.

The sessions sidebar only supports acting on one session at a time. Cleaning up after a busy day means archiving or deleting sessions one by one, each with its own context-menu round-trip and (for delete) its own confirm dialog. The Sessions settings page already has checkbox multi-select with batch delete, but the sidebar — where people actually manage sessions — has nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch session management belongs where the session list lives. The batch RPC path (`SessionCapability.deleteMany`) already exists and is used by the Sessions page; the sidebar just never adopted it. This change adds standard list multi-select UX on top of the existing menu and capability seams without touching gateway protocol or core.

## User Impact

- **Cmd/Ctrl-click** toggles a sidebar session row in and out of a selection; **shift-click** extends the selection from the anchor across the visible row order. Plain click clears the selection and opens the session as before.
- Right-clicking (or opening the `…` menu on) a selected row shows a **batch menu**: `Mark N as unread` / `Mark N as read`, `Move N to group`, `Archive N`, `Delete N…` — only actions that apply to every selected session. Single-session menus are unchanged.
- Right-clicking a row outside the selection retargets the menu to that row and drops the selection (standard behavior).
- **Batch delete** asks for one confirmation, uses the existing `sessions.deleteMany` path, and surfaces preserved dirty worktrees as a single summary alert (same policy as the Sessions page). Archive/delete are enabled only when every selected row is archivable (agent main sessions and active runs stay protected).
- Selected rows get a distinct highlight that stays readable next to the active-row highlight.
- New strings are translated across all 20 locales (`pnpm ui:i18n:sync`, fallbacks=0).

## Evidence

- Surface: `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` (selection state, click handling, batch dispatch), `ui/src/components/session-menu.ts` (batch mode), `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts` (batch targets carry `deleteTranscript`), `ui/src/styles/layout.css`, `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts` + generated bundles.
- Tests: `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` — cmd-click toggle + plain-click clear, shift-range across visible order, batch archive patches every selected key, batch delete via one confirm + `deleteMany` with `deleteTranscript`, unselected-row retarget. `ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts` — batch menu renders only count-labeled batch actions; `Mark N as read` aggregation.
- Testbox: `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts` → 2 files, 36 tests passed (lease `tbx_01kx8c6jdxfaya74b0n41xbr8e`).
- Testbox: `pnpm check:changed` → passed (exit 0, 9m0s, same lease).
- Testbox: `pnpm test ui/src/i18n` → passed (locale structural alignment covers the new keys across all bundles).
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.5`, thinking xhigh) on the source commit: one P1 — "generated locale bundles not synced" — which is addressed by the branch's follow-up i18n sync commit (the review was commit-scoped because the generated `.i18n` translation-memory diff exceeds the 180k review-bundle cap). No other findings.

target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine opencode` reported no accepted/actionable findings after the optional-chain cleanup.

## Proof

- Added regression coverage for Google/Gemini-vs-Vertex manifest env scoping: `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` alone is false for selected `gemini`, while `GEMINI_API_KEY` is true.
- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.
- Existing policy/credential tests still cover plugin allow/deny, disabled entries, keyless providers, raw plugin webSearch credentials, SecretRefs, and explicit provider selection.



### Follow-up Evidence - 2026-07-11

- Commit `cbd771ef20` rejects explicitly configured unknown web-search providers before top-level or nested credentials can satisfy the credential-presence audit.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 30 tests.
